_metadata.title: NavicEngine ECU Sensor Dictionary
_metadata.description: Human-readable interpretations for all 37 sensor variables found in the INCA ECU save-file CSV exports. Based on the NavicEngine README context (6-cylinder 7.6L DT diesel, dual-staged turbocharger, electro-hydraulic injectors) and standard ETAS INCA / ASCET naming conventions.
_metadata.dataset: NavicEngine — Diesel Engine Fault Diagnosis Dataset

time.description: Elapsed time from start of data recording session
time.note: Standard ECU logging timestamp. Present in all CSV files.

n.description: Engine rotational speed measured by the ECU
n.note: Verified against CSV values: ~1003 at 1000 RPM setpoint, ~1195 at 1200 RPM setpoint.

prs_tur_down.description: Air pressure measured downstream of the turbocharger turbine (exhaust side outlet)
prs_tur_down.note: Convention: prs_=pressure, tur=turbocharger, down=downstream. Values near atmospheric (~984) at idle.

prs_thr_up.description: Air pressure measured upstream of the throttle valve (intake manifold side)

prs_thr_up_sp.description: Target/commanded pressure upstream of the throttle valve from ECU
prs_thr_up_sp.note: _sp suffix = setpoint (commanded value). Usually tracks prs_thr_up closely.

prs_thr_down.description: Air pressure measured downstream of the throttle valve

prs_bpa.description: Absolute boost pressure (charge air pressure after turbocharger compressor)
prs_bpa.note: bpa = Boost Pressure Absolute. Key diagnostic variable for turbocharger performance.

prs_sp_bpa.description: Target/commanded boost pressure absolute from ECU
prs_sp_bpa.note: _sp suffix = setpoint. Comparison with prs_bpa reveals turbocharger system errors.

prs_bpa_dif.description: Difference between actual and setpoint boost pressure (or across a restriction)
prs_bpa_dif.note: _dif = differential. Could be prs_bpa - prs_sp_bpa or pressure drop across intercooler. High importance in sensor_mapping.json for FAULT_INJ_PRS and FAULT_SOI at higher speeds.

prs_cmpr_up.description: Air pressure measured upstream of the turbocharger compressor (fresh air inlet)
prs_cmpr_up.note: cmpr = compressor. Upstream of compressor ≈ atmospheric/ambient at the air filter inlet.

prs_cmpr_down.description: Air pressure measured downstream of the turbocharger compressor outlet
prs_cmpr_down.note: Compressor outlet pressure. Should correlate with prs_bpa (boost pressure) at similar locations.

prs_up_cmp_prot[0].description: Pressure sensor for compressor protection monitoring (inlet side)
prs_up_cmp_prot[0].note: prot = protection monitoring. Array [0] suggests single sensor. Used to detect compressor surge or restriction.

prs_eg[0].description: Pressure of exhaust gas in the exhaust manifold or system
prs_eg[0].note: eg = exhaust gas. Single sensor [0]. Key for detecting exhaust restriction or turbocharger turbine issues.

prs_eg_mes[0].note: _mes = measured. Likely the same physical variable as prs_eg[0] but from a different sensor or after signal processing.

egbp_mes[0].description: Measured back pressure in the exhaust system
egbp_mes[0].note: egbp = Exhaust Gas Back Pressure. Measured downstream of turbine or after treatment system.

fup_mes.description: Fuel rail pressure measured by the ECU sensor
fup_mes.note: fup = Fuel (rail) Pressure. Values ~5.6-7.9; too low for bar, too high for MPa. Likely in some scaled unit. _mes = measured.

fup.description: Fuel rail pressure (commanded or reported value)
fup.note: Without _mes suffix, this may be the commanded/expected fuel pressure vs the measured one (fup_mes).

fup_sp.description: Target fuel rail pressure commanded by ECU
fup_sp.note: _sp = setpoint. Comparison fup_sp vs fup_mes reveals fuel pressure control errors (relevant for FAULT_INJ_PRS).

pfu_mes.description: Measured pilot injection fuel quantity or pressure
pfu_mes.note: pfu may stand for 'Pilot Fuel' or 'Pressure Fuel'. Values (~5.2-8.5) overlap with fup_mes range, suggesting it could be a second fuel pressure sensor (low-pressure side) or pilot injection quantity.

pfu_l_mes.description: Low-pressure side fuel pressure or fuel quantity for pilot injection
pfu_l_mes.note: Values ~3850-4000 are an order of magnitude higher than pfu_mes/fup_mes. '_l' could indicate 'low pressure' circuit or a different physical measurement entirely. Significantly affected by FAULT_INJ_PRS and FAULT_SOI per sensor_mapping.json.

poil.note: poil = Pressure Oil. Values ~6849-6855, consistent with typical diesel engine oil pressure (68-69 bar × 100 or 6.8-6.9 MPa).

map.description: Absolute pressure in the intake manifold
map.note: Standard automotive MAP sensor. Reads ~1225-1226 at 1000 RPM, consistent with 1.2 bar absolute at idle for a turbocharged diesel.

map_mes.description: Measured MAP sensor reading (possibly redundant or post-processed)
map_mes.note: _mes = measured. Likely redundant with map from a different sensor channel.

soi_main1.description: Start of injection timing for the main injection event (cylinder 1 or reference)
soi_main1.note: soi = Start of Injection. Values ~0.63-0.68 in CSV — likely in ms or crank angle degrees × scaling. _main1 = main injection (not pilot).

soi_main1_bas.description: Base (calibrated) start of injection timing for main injection
soi_main1_bas.note: _bas = base value from ECU calibration maps. Represents the nominal timing before corrections.

soi_main1_tu.display_name: Start of Injection Main 1 Time Unit
soi_main1_tu.description: Start of injection timing expressed in time units or crank angle with per-cylinder correction
soi_main1_tu.note: _tu = Time Unit or Timing Unit. May represent the final (corrected) commanded timing.

soi_main1_chk_tu[0].display_name: SOI Main 1 Check Time Unit — Cylinder 1
soi_main1_chk_tu[0].description: Per-cylinder check of start of injection timing for cylinder 1
soi_main1_chk_tu[0].note: Array index [0] = Cylinder 1. _chk = check/monitor value. Used for cylinder-specific injection timing verification.

soi_main1_chk_tu[1].display_name: SOI Main 1 Check Time Unit — Cylinder 2
soi_main1_chk_tu[1].description: Per-cylinder check of start of injection timing for cylinder 2

soi_main1_chk_tu[2].display_name: SOI Main 1 Check Time Unit — Cylinder 3
soi_main1_chk_tu[2].description: Per-cylinder check of start of injection timing for cylinder 3

soi_main1_chk_tu[3].display_name: SOI Main 1 Check Time Unit — Cylinder 4
soi_main1_chk_tu[3].description: Per-cylinder check of start of injection timing for cylinder 4

soi_main1_chk_tu[4].display_name: SOI Main 1 Check Time Unit — Cylinder 5
soi_main1_chk_tu[4].description: Per-cylinder check of start of injection timing for cylinder 5

soi_main1_chk_tu[5].display_name: SOI Main 1 Check Time Unit — Cylinder 6
soi_main1_chk_tu[5].description: Per-cylinder check of start of injection timing for cylinder 6
soi_main1_chk_tu[5].note: Array index [5] = Cylinder 6. The inline-6 DT engine has 6 cylinders corresponding to indices [0..5].

ti_main1_bas.description: Base injection timing from ECU calibration for main injection
ti_main1_bas.note: ti = Timing. _bas = base calibration value. Overlaps with soi_main1 — may represent a different representation of injection timing.

ti_main1_tu.description: Injection timing for main injection expressed in time/crank-angle units
ti_main1_tu.note: _tu = Time Unit. Present in FAULT_INJ_DUR CSVs at 1000/1200 RPM but absent in NOMINAL and other faults, suggesting it is an injection-duration-specific variable.

ti_main1_tu_tmp.description: Temporary/intermediate injection timing value for main injection
ti_main1_tu_tmp.note: _tmp = temporary. Likely an intermediate calculation variable in the ECU injection timing computation. Not a direct sensor measurement. Present only in NOMINAL and FAULT_INJ_DUR CSVs.

ti_main1_tu_[0].display_name: Injection Timing Main 1 Time Unit Array
ti_main1_tu_[0].description: Per-cylinder injection timing for main injection (cylinder 1)
ti_main1_tu_[0].note: Underscore before [0] suggests this is a different ECU variable from ti_main1_tu — possibly an internal monitored value. Present only in FAULT_INJ_DUR CSVs.

amp_mes.description: Measured pressure in the charge air / intake system — exact sensor identity unclear
amp_mes.note: The abbreviation 'amp' is ambiguous in the INCA context. Numeric values (~984 at idle) are identical to prs_tur_down, prs_cmpr_up, and prs_up_cmp_prot[0] at 1000 RPM nominal, suggesting proximity to compressor inlet/ambient. amp could stand for 'Ambient Pressure', 'Air Mass Pressure', 'Absolute Manifold Pressure' (redundant with MAP), or something else. It is NOT 'Amplitude' as the values are pressure-range. Cannot resolve without original INCA database metadata. Included because sensor_mapping.json ranks it as the #1 most important sensor across multiple fault types.

amp_mes.issue: Abbreviation 'amp' has no standard INCA definition in the available documentation. Possible expansions include Ambient Pressure, Air Mass Pressure, or an internal ECU variable name. Values correlate perfectly with compressor upstream pressures at idle, but the sensor name alone is insufficient to determine the exact measurement point.
amp_mes.recommendation: Requires original INCA database export metadata or ETAS ASAP2/A2L file to resolve the exact sensor label and measurement channel.

pfu_mes.issue: 'pfu' could expand to 'Pilot Fuel' (injection parameter) or 'Pressure Fuel' (redundant with fup). Value range overlaps with fup_mes, making the distinction unclear. '_l' variant (pfu_l_mes) has 3-order-of-magnitude different values (~3900 vs ~5.7), suggesting fundamentally different physical quantities.
pfu_mes.recommendation: Requires A2L description or INCA measurement catalog to determine whether pfu refers to pressure, quantity, or an internal calculated value.

ti_main1_tu_tmp.issue: '_tmp' suffix suggests an intermediate ECU internal variable, not a direct sensor reading. Likely a temporary value in the injection timing calculation chain. Not a physical measurement.
ti_main1_tu_tmp.recommendation: Verify against ECU calibration data if this variable can be relied upon for diagnostics or if it should be excluded from sensor analysis.

ti_main1_tu_[0].issue: The underscore before the array index (tu_[0] vs tu[0]) is non-standard and suggests this may be a different variable array than ti_main1_tu. Only present in FAULT_INJ_DUR CSV files, indicating it may be a fault-specific monitoring variable rather than a general sensor.
ti_main1_tu_[0].recommendation: Confirm naming convention against INCA database export. Consider whether this should be treated as the same quantity as ti_main1_tu or a distinct variable.
